answer:
Use `promptfoo retry <evalId>` to re-run only the errored test cases from a specific eval. "Retry all ERROR results from a specific eval. This command finds test cases that resulted in errors (e.g., from network issues, rate limits, or API failures) and re-runs only those test cases." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

For example:

```sh
promptfoo retry eval-abc123
```

The retry updates the original eval in place. "Unlike `--filter-errors-only` which creates a new eval, `promptfoo retry` updates the original eval in place. Use `retry` when you want to fix errors in an existing eval without creating duplicates." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

If you want to retry the errors from the most recent eval instead of a specific one, use the eval flag: "The retry errors feature automatically finds ERROR results from the latest eval and re-runs only those test cases." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

```sh
promptfoo eval --retry-errors
```

Your original errors are kept if a retry fails: "If the retry fails, your original ERROR results are preserved. Old ERROR results are only removed after the retry succeeds." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]
